item.title: Plantoir 1.8.5
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.8.5
This update brings Windows from 1.7.2 up to date with everything the Mac got in 1.8.0 to 1.8.5.
BEFORE YOU UPDATE
- Deploy each section again to bring the new features to your sites. A site you deployed earlier keeps working exactly as it did. Runnable programs, quizzes, tickable checklists, My Progress, redrawn diagrams and pictures that no longer make the text jump all reach a site the next time you preview and deploy it. - Deploy each section again to bring diagrams back. Since late August, a site deployed to Netlify has shown each Mermaid diagram as the text it was written in, instead of drawing it. Deploying again draws them. Sites on Cloudflare or deployed to a folder were never affected, and neither was Preview. - Obsidian will ask whether you trust the author. When Plantoir offers to add Obsidian's add-ons for diagrams and graphs and you say yes, Obsidian asks, the first time each course opens with them, whether you trust the author of its pages. That is you. Click "Trust author and enable plugins". Pressing Enter chooses Restricted Mode, and the drawings then stay as text. - Rebuild and deploy your sites to size pictures. Every picture's size is now written into the page when the site is built, so the text stops jumping as pictures arrive on a slow first visit. A picture you gave a size yourself in your notes is drawn exactly as before. - The ready-made ICS3U course has changed. If you already created an ICS3U course from it, your copy stays as it is; the new version, with programs students can run, is what you get when you create one after updating. The ready-made courses' "What This Site Can Do" pages were also rewritten. - A course with a colon in its name that you started empty may not build. If you made it with an earlier version (for example "Physics: Mechanics") and the build says a section's front page cannot be read, open sectionN\index.md in Obsidian and put double quotes around the title on line 2. Courses made from now on are written that way already.
NOT YET ON WINDOWS
- Swift programs that students can run. A Swift code block still shows as code on the page, read-only; it is not run. The Mac can run them.
NEW
- Python programs students can run on the page (on Netlify or Cloudflare, programs that ask for input wait for a typed answer; on a folder or school web space, students type input before pressing Run). Add one line to a page's settings and the word "run" to a Python code block, and students get the program in an editor with Run, Stop and Reset, with nothing to install and no account. - Self-check quizzes. Write multiple choice, select all that apply, short answer and fill-in-the-blank questions in your notes; students check their own answers, with your explanation. It is practice, never a grade, and nothing leaves their browser. - Students can tick the checklists on your pages, and their ticks are remembered in their own browser. - My Progress: a page for each student's own progress, listing each page with a checklist under "Test of success", "Tests of success" or "Success criteria", with how many items are ticked. Units, classes and pages open to show their items. - Obsidian shows your diagrams and graphs. Once, before Obsidian opens, Plantoir offers to add the add-ons that draw them. Your answer applies to every course that has them, and Plantoir never changes add-ons you installed yourself. File, Settings, Obsidian holds the switch. - Claude Code and Codex know the new features, and every way a page can be written.
IMPROVED
- Get Ready for the Start of the Year shows the pages going into draft as a table (page, folder and why), with the warnings first. - Publish Pages and the assistant's plan no longer list curriculum expectation pages as "already visible". - Each overall expectation lists "When did we do this?". Maths on your sites no longer depends on another website. - Plantoir's activity record (used in problem reports) opens with your version number and says why Plantoir closed.
FIXED
- A folder you add in Course Settings appears on the site, with its own page in the sidebar and a page to copy. - Undo, pressed again once a page you edited is set back, takes the change off the list instead of getting stuck. - Hiding a class no longer keeps a page visible just because it is called "Curriculum Coverage"; only pages inside a curriculum folder stay visible. - In a club, the publish plan says "meeting" for a linked meeting it leaves alone. - A window remembered on a screen that has since been unplugged now reopens on a screen you can see. - No site loads a page-view counter nobody set up.
DOWNLOADS
File: PlantoirSetup.exe Size: 248.3 MB (260,328,160 bytes) SHA-256: 3718cbc3d217bd0601c7d2dd0a726f880fd7a4d13aeee8e6dcecca5eb65080aa File: Plantoir-win-x64.zip Size: 414.5 MB (434,632,904 bytes) SHA-256: 61bd101590a3a04bcb4ffb19d23a453789614f1617b128611933a59d5f197821
The SHA-256 lets your IT department verify the download is genuine.

item.title: Plantoir 1.7.2
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.7.2
This update brings Windows up to date with what the Mac got in 1.7.2.
Publish Pages, Hide Pages and Publish Class for a Date, in the Section menu, now show the pages in a table: each page, its folder and what will happen to it, with a one-line summary above. Every page is listed, the table scrolls, and you can sort it by any column. Press Enter to go ahead or Escape to cancel, as before.
On your class sites, each page inside an open folder of "Navigate this site" has a small dot before it, and a long title that wraps onto a second line now lines up under its first word, so it no longer looks like two pages. The dot stays visible in a High Contrast theme. Your sites pick this up the next time you preview or deploy.
Schedule a deploy no longer asks you to keep a laptop plugged in. It says what matters: the PC must be on and awake then, with the lid open. On battery a PC goes to sleep sooner, so keep it awake until then.
When you make room for classes and other classes have to move, the assistant now tells you before you press Go that Undo will not take it back. Your backup is the way out.
When you ask Claude or Codex to write your How I Teach page for a course you keep only for reference, the plan now says the course stays as it is, instead of promising a change that would then be refused.
Plantoir now opens no narrower than its smallest size, so at 150% display scaling the Preview, Deploy and Browser buttons are all there from the first launch.
Fixed: after Re-date Classes stops part way, the answer now names the pages that were already re-dated. If the very first change cannot be saved, it says nothing was changed. Fixed: Plantoir's activity record (used in problem reports) now says "took part of the last change back" after a partial Undo, and says what happened after a Make Room, or a publish or hide that stopped part way, instead of "changed nothing".

item.title: Plantoir 1.7.1
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.7.1
This update is for Windows only, and brings Windows up to date with everything the Mac got in 1.5.0, 1.6.0, 1.7.0 and 1.7.1.
A menu bar now runs across the top of the window. Everything you can do to a course or section is in it, greyed out when it cannot be done right now, with keyboard shortcuts shown beside the items. File > Open Recent lists the working folders you have opened. The things you used to ask the assistant for are in the Section menu too: Publish Pages, Hide Pages, Publish Class for a Date, Rebuild Preview, Undo Last Change, Add Next Class, Re-date Classes, Make Room for Classes and Class Dates. Each shows you what it will do before it does it.
File > Settings is now one window, with Assistant, Deploying and Preview. Your Cloudflare Account ID lives in Deploying and nowhere else; course settings and the New Course panel show it, with a button to open Settings. Help > Plantoir Help (F1) opens plantoir.app.
When you deploy, Plantoir asks about class pages students can already see that are dated after your next class. You can hide the ones you tick, or keep them all. Tomorrow's class, published the evening before, is never asked about.
Preview can pick up where you left off. In File > Settings > Preview, choose whether Preview opens your site's front page or the page you were last reading in that section. Hold Alt to get the other choice for one press. The Preview button and Section menu always say what will happen. Nothing changes unless you ask for it.
A page can now print as a handout. Course Settings has a Printing section, and Print in the preview opens the page in your web browser, ready to print. You can draw diagrams in your notes and add graphs of functions that students can drag and zoom. Both print whole, in black on white. Claude and Codex are told how to write these pages: on request, Plantoir writes a short guide into your working folder, and asks before adding to a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md you already keep there.
Windows also follows its own conventions more closely. Escape closes every window and is never trapped, a button that cannot be pressed never looks like the main one, and the Delete key (or the minus button) removes the course, section or backup you have selected, after asking. All Backups can be sorted and has a right-click menu. Dialog titles are clearer, and the smallest text is a little bigger. Right-click a course or section for Revise With, then Claude, Codex or the local assistant.
Fixed: if you set a scheduled deploy again while an earlier run is still working, the new one now waits its turn instead of being lost. A scheduled deploy also brings the folder's tools up to date by itself first. Closing Plantoir while a folder is being got ready now waits for it to finish, then quits. When you hide a page, the preview now rebuilds, as it does when you publish one. When Claude or Codex's preview cannot be built, the answer now says why in a sentence. A failed build is no longer blamed on Netlify just because the number 429 appeared in its output.

item.title: Plantoir 1.4.5
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.4.5
This update is for Windows only.
The first window after an update used to be missing for about two minutes while Plantoir got your folder ready. Now the window appears at once, with a notice that says the folder is being got ready and that Preview and Deploy wait for it. They come back on their own the moment it finishes: about 15 to 20 seconds on a typical laptop, longer on a slow disk.
When Claude or Codex schedules a deploy and names classes like "Unit 2, Day 3", the title is no longer cut in half. Class titles are separated by semicolons, so a comma inside a title stays where you put it.
When Claude or Codex rebuilds a preview or publishes a page while that section is being deployed, the answer now says the section is being deployed, so the preview cannot be built until that finishes. Before, it only said the preview could not be built.

item.title: Plantoir 1.4.4
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.4.4
Plantoir now says "deploy" for putting your website online and "publish" only for marking a page to be included. The words are kept apart everywhere you read them: in the app, in what the assistant says, in the starter pages a new course comes with, and on plantoir.app.
Type "schedule a deploy for tomorrow at 6:30 am" to the assistant and it sets that up for you to agree to; "schedule a deploy" with no time asks you for one and never deploys right away; "cancel that scheduled deploy" or the shelf's "Cancel scheduled deploy" cancels it.
"Start a new unit with the next class" and "Add three more days to Unit 2" are answered by the assistant exactly as you say them. A request it cannot be sure about is pointed at the wording that does it, rather than adding a page you did not ask for.
A Claude or Codex session opened from Plantoir keeps hold of the course it was opened from, the way the built-in assistant does: its backup is kept, a second session on the same course is refused, and renaming or restoring the course waits until the session ends.
A deploy no longer starts while that section is still being deployed, including by a deploy that was set for later: it tells you to try again when that has finished. A scheduled deploy's notification now reads "deployed on its own to ...", and says that your website has the new pages. Dismissing that notice in Plantoir also takes it out of Windows' notification centre.
The title bar follows your Windows light or dark setting.
An update marked important offers Install and Reopen only, and is offered even if you had skipped that version. An update offer that could not be shown, because Plantoir was still starting or another dialog was in front, is no longer counted as you saying "not now"; it is offered again a little later.
The About window says "Grow a class website."

item.title: Plantoir 1.4.3
item.description:
New in Plantoir 1.4.3
Type "publish unit 4, day 3", "schedule a deploy at 6:30 am" or "cancel that scheduled deploy" to the assistant and it is answered straight away. "Schedule a deploy" without a time asks you for the time, and never deploys right away.
Claude and Codex can change a course while its preview is open. They are asked to wait only while Plantoir is actually building that course's website. A change made while a preview is open is saved straight away: press Stop Preview, then Preview, to see it. If a deploy closes a preview, the section says "Closed for a deploy" instead of telling you something went wrong.
"Revise with Claude" can now work on every course in your working folder.
A scheduled deploy now tells you how it went, in a notification, every time.
When two pages have the same name, asking the assistant to publish one asks which you meant, naming each with its folder. When a change to several pages stops part way, the assistant says plainly that only part of it was made. When making room for extra classes cannot finish every page, Plantoir names the pages to look over.
The smaller assistant now stops a long answer sooner, but on some requests it can still take up to about 80 seconds before saying its answer was cut off. Nothing it started is carried out when that happens.
A screen reader now names every button that shows only an icon, and tells a course kept for reference from the course you are teaching.
Course Settings no longer protects a folder from removal just because Plantoir guessed it held your class pages.
Class dates remembered with an impossible year are asked for again instead of being believed.
From this version on, when Plantoir offers an update it shows what is new in every version since yours.
